title: The Challenges of Strain Analysis for Electron Tomography
content: Geometric phase analysis (GPA) leverages Fourier space information to autonomously quantify displacement, strain, and grain orientation in atomic lattices. GPA is routinely used to retrieve these quantities in two dimensions when atomic structure is resolved, including in S/TEM micrographs [1, 2]. GPA is also applied to three-dimensional (3D) datasets [3], illuminating the internal strain and grain boundaries. The extension of GPA to 3D requires three linearly independent Bragg peaks, implicitly defining a 3D reference lattice and capturing all atomic displacements.
